title: Distribute Elements Into Two Arrays II
summary: Given a 1-indexed integer array nums, distribute its elements into two arrays arr1 and arr2 using n operations.
statement: Given a 1-indexed integer array nums, distribute its elements into two arrays arr1 and arr2 using n operations. Initially, nums[1] goes to arr1 and nums[2] to arr2. For each subsequent element, append it to arr1 if it has more elements greater than the current number, to arr2 if fewer, and to the smaller array if equal. Ties break by appending to arr1. The result is the concatenation of arr1 and arr2.
constraints: nums contains at least two positive integers.
Start arrays with nums[0] and nums[1]; each later value goes where strictly more existing elements are greater.
Equal greater-counts choose the shorter array, with a remaining size tie choosing the first; return first followed by second.
hints: Greater-than counts equal array length minus the number of values at or below the current value.
Coordinate-compress values and maintain one Fenwick frequency tree per result array.
Query each tree through current rank; compare length-prefixCount, then apply size and first-array ties; append and update.
Fenwick prefix frequencies give exact greater counts, and the conditional sequence directly implements every distribution rule in priority order.
editorial: Fenwick prefix frequencies give exact greater counts, and the conditional sequence directly implements every distribution rule in priority order.

tests.explanation: The first three goes to the first array by the size tie; the second three goes to the second, producing [2,3,1,3].
Three and one go to the first array by greater counts; two then goes to the second, producing [5,3,1,14,2].
